content.question: How does SHAP compute a feature's contribution?
options: It computes the gradients of the prediction with respect to each input and accumulates them along a path from a baseline.
It randomly permutes the feature's values and measures how much the model's performance drops as a result.
It measures the feature's marginal contribution in every possible coalition of features and averages these contributions over all of them.
It fits a single global linear surrogate model to the data and uses each coefficient as the feature's contribution.
It removes the feature from the data, retrains the model, and reports the drop in accuracy as its contribution.
content.answer: It measures the feature's marginal contribution in every possible coalition of features and averages these contributions over all of them.
